statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail rises three points to 24%, one point below the block threshold, after the US cash open reversed the overnight rally: NQ futures traded 30,626.50-30,648.75 near the 14:26Z research cutoff, roughly 0.2% lower on the day and within about 50 points of the 30,590.00 session low, some 525 points under the 31,151.50 high. ISM Manufacturing printed 54.5 with a Prices index of 77.9, the 10-year Treasury yield reached 5.34%, its highest since 2002, and VIX gained 5.4% to 17.22.
recommendation: Tail moves to 24% and remains inside the watch band. Price holding near the session low with the 10-year at a 24-year high, WTI 1.5% firmer at 91.76 and VIX 5.4% higher are genuine amplifiers, which is why Tail sits at the top of the band. They are offset by the fact that the index is only about 0.2% below its 30,698.75 previous close, so the 561-point decline completed a large retracement of the overnight advance rather than extending a one-way path beyond prior-day value, and a modest bounce off the low is in progress. Micron's record quarter and raised fiscal-2027 guidance conflict with the bearish tape; under this contract conflicting evidence raises Stress rather than Tail. Stress is 78% and Confidence 87%. The narrow danger window spans the post-ISM repricing while price sits near the session low.
headline: Tail 24% at the watch-band top as the cash open reverses the overnight rally; yields at a 24-year high hold Stress at 78%
body:
The observed Nasdaq-100 picture has changed materially since the previous publication. At 13:19Z NQ futures were 0.39% higher near 30,819.50; by the 14:26Z research cutoff they traded 30,626.50-30,648.75, about 0.2% lower on the day, within roughly 50 points of a 30,590.00 session low and some 525 points below the 31,151.50 high. The cash-index reading is consistent: the Nasdaq-100 index stood at 30,352.41, down 0.18%, against a 30,302.41-30,576.44 range. The 13:30Z open began higher and faded steadily, and the 14:00Z ISM Manufacturing release accelerated that fade. The headline PMI was 54.5 against 54.6 in August and a consensus near 55.2, a ninth consecutive month of expansion, but the composition was the market-moving part: New Orders improved to 55.3 while the Prices index jumped to 77.9 from 71.1. That inflationary component reinforced an already hawkish rates channel. The 10-year Treasury yield reached 5.34% intraday, its highest since 2002, and sat near 5.33%; H.15 placed the 2-year at 4.89% and the 30-year at 5.59% as of 29 September. WTI added 1.5% to 91.76 and VIX rose 5.4% to 17.22 inside a 16.21-17.59 range.

Four amplifiers are therefore aligned: price near a session extreme, yields at multidecade highs, firmer oil and a rising volatility premium. That combination is what lifts Tail to 24%, the top of the watch band. It stops short of the block threshold for three evidence-based reasons. First, the decline is a round trip rather than a breakdown: at roughly 0.2% under the 30,698.75 previous close the 561-point fall retraced the overnight advance without establishing acceptance below prior-day value, which is mean reversion working rather than failing. Second, a modest bounce of some 36-58 points off the low is under way, so price is not pinned at the extreme. Third, the catalyst set conflicts: Micron reported record fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of 54.2 billion dollars with adjusted earnings of 33.42 dollars per share, both above consensus, and guided fiscal 2027 higher on sustained AI memory demand, yet the shares were little changed. Under this contract conflicting evidence raises Stress and lowers directional conviction rather than mechanically raising Tail, and the absolute VIX level of 17.22 remains low.

Stress advances to 78%, high but inside the band, reflecting the volatility premium, the multidecade-high rates backdrop, firmer crude and a 561-point intraday reversal. Confidence is 87%: current futures and cash-index levels were cross-checked against two independent feeds, the ISM release was read from the primary ISM report, yields from the Federal Reserve H.15 release and the calendar from a structured economic-calendar source. One point is withheld because the shared Finviz context file was stale, with a collection timestamp of 29 September and partial status, and because tick-level NQ path data is not directly available. Independent research proceeded without it, as the contract requires.

The forward path is governed by one near checkpoint and one large scheduled one. The near checkpoint is whether the post-ISM impulse extends through the 30,590.00 low without retracement or whether the session recovers toward the previous close; conditional Tail decays from 24% through the US afternoon to 17% in the quiet Asian hours on the assumption that retracements remain available. The scheduled checkpoint is the September employment report at 12:30Z on 2 October, where payrolls are seen near 90,000 against 162,000 prior and the unemployment rate near 4.1%, with ADP having reported 90,000 private jobs on 30 September. Conditional Stress rises to the extreme band at 82-83% for the release and the hour after it, while conditional Tail is deliberately held at 24%: event importance and surprise magnitude do not by themselves establish a persistent no-retracement path, and the observed path will be scored once it exists.

lookbackSummary: Across the preceding 24 hours Claude published an unbroken watch-band regime. Tail ran between 20% and 25%, touching the 25% block threshold once in the 06:00Z hour on a trend-up reading before easing back to 20-22% when that structure failed to persist. Stress climbed steadily from 69% to a 76% peak in the 10:00Z hour and held in the mid-70s, and Confidence was stable at 87-89% throughout. Dominant mode was mixed in 22 of the 24 hours. The sequence describes a market absorbing a high-rates environment inside a range rather than trending through it, which is the baseline the current cash-session reversal is measured against.
outlookSummary: The near path turns on whether the post-ISM fade extends through the 30,590.00 session low without a retracement or whether price recovers toward the 30,698.75 previous close. Conditional Tail holds at 24% for the current and next hour while price sits near the extreme, eases to 21-23% through the US afternoon, ticks back to 22% for the 19:00Z power hour on late-session continuation or reversal risk, then decays to 17-19% across the post-close and Asian hours as liquidity thins and the assumed regime becomes a quiet consolidation. From the 05:00Z European handover the conditional path rebuilds to 20-22% on calendar proximity rather than observed structure, ahead of the September employment report at 12:30Z on 2 October. For the release hour and the hour after it, conditional Stress moves to the extreme band at 82-83% while conditional Tail is held at 24%: under this contract event importance and surprise magnitude inform Stress and Confidence, and a pathological price path must be observed before it is scored.
